brief_bullets: A Kolkata court has remanded seven individuals to ten days of police custody following a tragic stampede at a Durga Puja pandal that occurred during heavy rainfall on Saturday evening. Local authorities have formally registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, signaling a rigorous investigation into potential negligence regarding crowd management and safety protocols at the site. The incident, which unfolded around 7:40 pm, has prompted intense scrutiny of the organizers' adherence to safety regulations during one of the city's most significant cultural festivals. As investigators work to determine the specific lapses that led to the fatal crush, the legal proceedings against the accused highlight a growing institutional demand for stricter accountability in managing large-scale public gatherings. This development underscores the precarious balance between maintaining traditional festivities and ensuring the physical security of thousands of attendees in high-density urban environments.
why_it_matters_bullets: This case sets a critical legal precedent for event liability in India, likely forcing organizers to adopt more stringent safety compliance measures to avoid criminal prosecution for crowd-related disasters.

Beyond questioning the immediate operational protocols of a single festival committee, the disaster exposes systemic vulnerabilities in state-level crowd management and risk anticipation during massive public gatherings. The administration's delayed and uncoordinated emergency response has intensified public scrutiny over governmental preparedness, forcing a thorough re-evaluation of safety regulations at large-scale cultural events across West Bengal. stories.primary_headline: Explained|Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA

primary_source.headline: Explained|Govt caps trade margins on 137 cancer drugs at 30%: NPPA
primary_source.content: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers has announced a price cap of 30 per cent on the trade margins of 137 cancer medicines, over the cost of the drug at the first point, either to a stockist/distributor or the hospital. These margins will apply when the drugs are sold directly to them by a manufacturer.&nbsp;The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA), in an order dated October 17, has directed manufacturers to submit the revised MRP within seven days. "The revised prices shall come into effect from November 9," the gazette notification stated.&nbsp;Impact on cancer drug pricesAn analysis of pharmaceutical market data indicates that non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs carry an average trade mark-up of approximately 170 per cent, with mark-ups of up to 700 per cent in certain cases, according to an NPPA meeting conducted earlier. This order is expected to reduce the MRP of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs by 70 per cent, depending on their current price structures.&nbsp;The 137 identified non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy drugs used for treating over 20 types of cancers, denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, pegfilgrastim, which is used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients and bevacizumab, which is the approved drug to treat colon, ovarian, and cervical cancer. With this notification, MRP of widely used anti-cancer drugs such as pembrolizumab, durvalumab and osimertinib is expected to become more accessible for cancer patients.Anti-cancer drug prices to come down as govt caps trade margins at 30%Centre caps trade margins on cancer medicines at 30% of MRPMarket overview: scheduled vs non-scheduled drugsCurrently, the anti-cancer drugs market comprises nearly 225 drugs and 500 formulations, with an annual turnover of around Rs 12,500 crore. Of this, scheduled cancer drugs that come under price control account for approximately Rs 2,250 crore, with the balance comprising non-scheduled drugs.To ensure that these life-saving medicines remain available, manufacturers of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs will be required to maintain their current production levels. NPPA has clearly stated: "The manufacturers of the formulations are required to maintain the present production levels. Any manufacturer intending to lower the average monthly production levels will seek prior permission from NPPA. Further, any manufacturer intending to discontinue production of the above-said formulations shall furnish information to NPPA."&nbsp;How is the new price calculated?The manufacturers of non–scheduled formulations, selling branded or generic or both the versions of formulations at MRP higher than the MRP should revise their prices using this formula:&nbsp; MRP of the product = Price to Stockist or Price to Distributor x {1 + (Trade Margin/(100 − Trade Margin))} + Applicable GST.&nbsp;Citing an example, NPPA explained: For a non-scheduled anti-cancer formulation with current MRP: Rs 300 + Applicable GST. However, the price to a distributor is Rs 70. Maximum allowable revised MRP as per formula shall be: Rs70x{1+(30/(100−30))} = Rs 100 + Applicable GST.&nbsp;The notification has also clarified: "All the existing manufacturers of formulations having MRP lower than the MRP so computed … shall maintain their existing MRP."

stories.primary_headline: EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23

primary_source.headline: EC-SIR row | People's Movement march seeking Gyanesh Kumar's removal on October 23
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The 'People Against SIR', a coalition of various organisations, on Sunday announced a ‘People’s March to Reclaim Democracy’ on October 23 across India demanding removal and prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, scrapping of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and restoration of voters whose names have been deleted.With the slogan ‘Har Haath Mein Tiranga, Har Gali Jantar Mantar’ (In Every Hand Tricolor, Every Street is Jantar Mantar), the coalition of civil society organisations, farmer unions, trade unions, students and youth organisations, academicians, artistes and activists said the protest marches with tricolor in their hands will be held at tehsil, district, state and national level.Nothing can save CEC; SIR must be suspended forthwith: CongressThe coalition, which included actor-activist Prakash Raj, Kisan Sabha leader P Krishnaprasad and CPI(ML)L leader N Sai Balaji, said the ‘People's March’ will not request police permission anywhere while "strictly warning" police, paramilitary and prisons against using the "brute state force" against peaceful protesters.&nbsp;If the march is blocked by police, it said, the protesters will peacefully hold the People's Parliament and disperse later after singing the national anthem.Claiming that the CEC helped the BJP to remain in power, it recalled that the Supreme Court has maintained that it did not upheld alteration of Form 6 used for inclusion of new voters.&nbsp;“Gyanesh Kumar has violated his Constitutional pledge and must be prosecuted. But the Prime Minister himself is protecting the criminal...Without Parliament impeaching CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the Prime Minister cannot come out of the full-blown constitutional standoff,” it said.Calling upon farmers, workers, daily wage earners, traders, entrepreneurs, journalists, advocates, teachers, employees, artists, intellectuals, women, youth, students, adivasis, dalits and minorities to join the march, a statement said its demands include comprehensive electoral reforms, proportional representation, curb money/muscle power and legalise state funding of polls.The statement alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah have misused the Election Commission and erased the voting rights of 13.41 crore citizens through SIR.

stories.primary_headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction

primary_source.headline: Huge sand deposits remain utilised in Keralam even as state laments over Tamil Nadu's restriction
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state. According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of&nbsp; 30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed. The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation. Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments. The silt accumulation in the water bodies, which reduced the water holding capacity, has been found to be a reason for flash floods in the state. Keralam, which requires up to 30 million metric tonnes of sand annually, has been highly dependent on Tamil Nadu for rocks to sand. Hence the restriction by the neighbouring state has led to an acute scarcity in Keralam, which already led to almost three times cost escalation. Major infrastructure projects like the ongoing expansion of Vizhinjam international seaport and national highway were reportedly feeling the heat. Desilting of the water bodies is hence considered to have multiple benefits ranging from addressing construction material shortage to flood mitigation. Tamil Nadu bans transportation of rough stones to other states; Kerala seeks review The state government was forced to impose a ban on river sand mining in 2016 in view of the massive unregulated sand mining which even diverted the direction of flow of rivers at many places. Hence, the state has been depending on manufactured sand for construction. The stringent regulations for quarries have also&nbsp; led to the number of quarries coming down around 220 from 3800 ten years back, according to the Keralam Mining and Crushing Owners Association. Even as the state government initiated steps for desilting at a couple of dams like the Mangalam dam in Palakkad and introduced stringent norms for regulated river sand mining following the 2018-19 floods, those steps went into troubled waters&nbsp; owing to allegations of over exploitation and ecological concerns. Industry sources said that since the chances of Tamil Nadu easing the restrictions was remote, the state government should proactively take steps to address the crisis.&nbsp; Natural river sand offers a better construction quality than manufactured sand. Hence the government should take steps for regulated desilting and river sand mining," said Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India general convener general. However, environmental expert V Subashchandrabose points out that even as scientific desilting and river sand mining could be allowed, the state should popularise alternative&nbsp; construction methods that could reduce the dependence on natural resources.

brief_bullets: Thiruvananthapuram: While Keralam suffers acute shortage of construction materials owing to the restriction imposed by Tamil Nadu government in transporting construction materials, huge quantities of construction materials are remaining unutilised in the rivers and dams in the state.

According to a data presented by the state government in the assembly, after the 2018-19 floods it was evaluated that 43 of the 44 rivers in Keralam alone had a sand and silt deposit of  30.17 million cubic metre that could be removed.
The capacity of 15 of the 81 dams in the state alone came down by an average of 13.8 percent owing to the silt accumulation.

Huge sand deposits in Kerala rivers remain untapped Studies have found that the carrying capacity of Vebanad lake, the largest lake in Keralam, came down by up to 85 percent owing to reasons like silt deposit as well as encroachments.
why_it_matters_bullets: Underscores accelerating climate extremes, increasing long-term operational strain on public infrastructure and utility grids.

stories.primary_headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row

primary_source.headline: Aamir Khan meets Raj Thackeray amid nephew Imran's exit notice row
primary_source.content: Mumbai: Actor-filmmaker Aamir Khan met Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) president Raj Thackeray at his residence in Mumbai on Sunday.The details of the meeting were not immediately known.The meeting comes days after Aamir Khan's nephew and actor Imran Khan was served a notice by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO), directing him to leave India by October 28. Imran had reportedly participated in the October 10 protests at August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.The 43-year-old Imran Khan is a US citizen and an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder.'Leave India': Imran Khan moves Bombay HC against 'illegal, bad in law' notice by Mumbai police, FRRO issues him show-cause noticeHe has challenged the notice in the Bombay High Court, which is expected to hear the matter this week. The plea is expected to be mentioned for an urgent hearing before a division bench comprising Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna.“The notice has been issued without disclosing any reasons, supporting material, or specific statutory contravention. It was issued without inquiry, a show-cause notice, or any opportunity for the Petitioner (Khan) to respond to the alleged violations,” the plea stated.The FRRO issued the notice under Sections 7 and 29 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, directing Imran Khan to leave India by October 28, 2026.
